In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''toric stack''' is a [[stack (mathematics)|stacky]] generalization of a [[toric variety]]. More precisely, a toric stack is obtained by replacing in the construction of a toric variety a step of taking [[GIT quotient]]s with that of taking [[quotient stack]]s. Consequently, a toric variety is a coarse approximation of a toric stack. A '''toric orbifold''' is an example of a toric stack.
